Resolved by rebuilding the tab strip as a hop timeline. 'Sent to Provider', 'Final Response' and 'Provider Details' are gone; the log detail now has two modes, Conversation (what was said) and Trace (the wire). The Trace renders one node per hop in order — You sent / Attempt N per provider attempt / You received — with each fidelity change on the edge between the hops that produced it, so the old 'Step' column pointing at another tab is unnecessary. Each node expands to its own endpoint, key, outbound headers, request body, outbound body, error body, response body and response headers. Two mislabelings found and fixed while doing it: the top node no longer implies the stored IR is the client's body (it isn't stored, and the node says so), and the final node's body is labelled 'recorded before conversion to <format>' for non-OpenAI clients because the log holds the IR, not the egress bytes. Sync path: when any content block is untranslatable (thinking, redacted_thinking, server-tool, fallback), the whole native content list rides the response passthrough under 'content' and the Anthropic egress restores it 1:1 — Map.merge(built, provider_passthrough) already prefers it, so no egress change. Whole list rather than just the lost blocks because the reduction concatenates text, destroying boundaries. Carried only when something was lost, so ordinary responses don't record a false 'content dropped' for OpenAI-family clients. 5 new tests, 1101 pass. DodoRouter.Logs.CacheRegression.classify/1 — pure, I/O-free, in KeyHealth.classify style. Takes a session's ordered logs, returns :healthy | :insufficient_data | {:regressed, finding} where finding names diverged_at, through, pinned_read, turns and uncached_growth.

Keyed on read-vs-input rather than the epic's stated cache_write growth: cache_write_tokens is NULL on 733/740 dev rows, so a write test would be blind (noted on the epic). Cuts the session into comparable runs first — same provider+model (caches are model-scoped) and gaps within the 1h TTL — then looks for a streak of >=3 consecutive turns that fail to read back more than the turn before, over >2048 tokens of new input. A read stuck at 0 counts only if the run cached earlier, so sessions with no caching at all stay silent.

12 unit tests including the AGENTS.md breakpoint signature, the collapse-to-zero case, and both token conventions. Verified against all 6 real dev sessions with 3+ logs: no false positives. Caveat: the dev DB holds no known-broken session to replay, so the positive case is the documented signature encoded as a fixture rather than captured logs.

Session list marks regressed sessions; the session view opens with a notice naming the diverging turn (linked, and the turn itself is ringed in the timeline), how many turns stalled, the pinned read, and how much input was re-sent at full price. A collapsible prefix diff shows the region both requests share — the part that was supposed to come back byte-identical — rendered with TextDiff at line granularity.

Logs.cache_verdicts/2 feeds the list: one query selecting only the six columns the classifier reads, so a page of 20 sessions does not load 20 sessions' worth of bodies. 5 new LiveView tests, 1118 pass.

Both children shipped. A session whose cached prefix stops hitting is now detected by Logs.CacheRegression and surfaced in the session list and view, naming the diverging turn and diffing the shared prefix.

One gap against the epic's original acceptance criteria, worth knowing: the operator is alerted where they already look, but nothing pushes at them — they still have to open the sessions page. Pushing anomalies is dodo_router-ajp.3 (Attention panel), which this now feeds.

All three streaming controllers now pass request_id: into dispatch_streaming, so the x-request-id the client was handed is the request_id on the log row. Four integration tests over the real HTTP path: one per streaming endpoint (OpenAI, Anthropic, Responses) plus sync as a regression guard — all three streaming ones failed before the fix, sync passed. 1122 tests.
